item.title: Geometry-induced chaos and scaling near two singular limits of an eye-shaped billiard
item.description: arXiv:2610.29128v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate how boundary geometry controls the coexistence of regular and chaotic motion in a static, eye-shaped billiard. A single control parameter continuously deforms the smooth, strictly convex boundary between two singular geometric limits. Across the sampled parameter range, chaotic layers coexist with regular islands and invariant curves that restrict phase-space transport. We derive analytical conditions for the existence of diagonal period-two orbits and determine the stability transitions of the axial period-two trajectories. We also establish the existence of invariant caustics near the boundary for every finite positive value of the control parameter. Numerical simulations reveal a nonmonotonic dependence of the average maximal Lyapunov exponent on the control parameter, withthe strongest sampled instability occurring at an intermediate geometry. The mean squared-angle envelope width associated with the sampled chaotic component decreases toward both singular limits, following power laws with fitted exponents of opposite signs and magnitudes close to two thirds. We further characterize a geometric response function and discuss the resulting analogy with continuous critical behavior. Our findings show how geometric deformation governs orbital stability, barriers to chaotic transport, and scaling properties in conservative billiard dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Anne K\'etri P. da Fonseca, Edson D. Leonel, Diego F. M. Oliveira

item.title: Eclipse Observables for Navigation in Cislunar Space
item.description: arXiv:2610.28669v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Autonomous navigation independent of Earth-based tracking remains a challenge for spacecraft operating in cislunar space. This paper proposes onboard eclipse detection as an opportunistic measurement set to supplement the state estimation of cislunar trajectories. Penumbral and umbral entry and exit times detected from standard power telemetry are formulated as implicit zero-measurements on the boundaries of second-order shadow cones computed from planetary ephemerides. These observables are processed in an unscented Kalman filter. The event-time uncertainty that weights each measurement is derived from physical sources excluded in the spherical body model, including telemetry sampling, Earth's atmosphere, and topography/oblateness of the occulting body. The approach is demonstrated both in simulation for an $L_1$ halo orbit and with flight telemetry and orbit determination products from the CAPSTONE spacecraft during the January 2026 lunar eclipse, where umbral contacts timed directly from the power telemetry agree with the geometric contacts to within one sample interval. In both cases, hardware-free eclipse event timing shows utility in uncertainty reduction, especially as the initial solution quality is degraded.
item.dc:creator: Ian M. Down, James McElreath, Manoranjan Majji

item.title: Stochastic resonance in time-delayed bistable active particles
item.description: arXiv:2610.29601v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate analytically and numerically stochastic resonance in an underdamped active (Ornstein--Uhlenbeck) particle confined in a bistable potential with time-delayed feedback and subjected to an additional (non-thermal) white-noise source. Restricting the analysis to the active-noise-dominated bistable regime, with sufficiently short delay and active-noise correlation times, we develop a perturbative theory that yields analytical expressions for both the escape rate and the spectral power amplification within the framework of linear-response theory, without invoking detailed balance. The analytical predictions are in qualitative agreement with direct numerical simulations throughout the perturbative regime. We show that a moderate increase in the active-noise correlation time can enhance the stochastic-resonance response, in marked contrast to previous results for overdamped passive systems driven by colored noise. Conversely, the addition of white noise weakens the resonant response and shifts its optimum toward lower active-noise intensities. Time-delayed feedback further alters the matching condition between the escape rate and the driving frequency while preserving the resonant mechanism. Beyond the perturbative regime, we find that finite-memory effects progressively broaden the resonance profile and substantially decrease its amplitude. Overall, these results provide new insight into the combined role of inertia, activity, environmental fluctuations, and time delayed feedback in stochastic resonance in nonequilibrium systems.
item.dc:creator: Antonio A. Valido, Mattia Coccolo, Miguel A. F. Sanju\'an

item.title: Reduction of Decaying Navier--Stokes Turbulence to the Quantum Pendulum
item.description:
arXiv:2607.05745v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The statistics of a classical flow is a problem of quantum mechanics in loop space, and not by analogy: the loop functional of any flow is the loop-ordered exponential of the covariant derivative $\partial+\mathrm{i}v/
u$. We follow this representation from the Navier--Stokes equation to the Euler ensemble, the fixed point of the loop equation regularized by polygons with $N$ sides. Near the turning angle $ eta=\pi$ an exact operator identity, followed by an asymptotic continuum step and without a saddle-point approximation, reduces the ensemble to two quantum pendulums, the Mathieu equation; this supersedes our earlier WKB evaluation. A Monte Carlo simulation up to $N=10^5$ confirms the reduction. Extreme turbulence has singularities at small scales, and, as in quantum field theory, we define it by this regularization and a renormalization: the leading power of $N$ is removed, and the turbulent viscosity $	ilde
u$ remains as the single physical scale. This is a proposed definition of turbulence at infinite Reynolds number; its continuum spectrum is computed under a stated convergence condition, and its identification with physical turbulence is a hypothesis. The energy spectrum is a function of $\kappa=k\sqrt{	ilde
u(t+t_0)}$ that falls as $1/k$ and then as $k^{-2}$. At $\kappa=\sqrt2$ it has a weak nonanalyticity: its second derivative diverges logarithmically. At a fixed wave number the decay is therefore singular at the finite time $t_*=2/(	ilde
u k^2)-t_0$, when $t_*>0$, and the vorticity correlations oscillate in space with the period $\sqrt2\,\pi\sqrt{	ilde
u(t+t_0)}$. Of the limits of the ensemble with structure, only the pendulum limit is taken at a critical point and has a bulk dissipation that vanishes with the viscosity. A companion paper compares it with simulations and experiments.

item.title: Physics is the Best Teacher: Consistency Learning for Time-Invariant Operators of Chaotic Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.04108v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Accelerating the prediction of long-term behavior in chaotic systems is crucial in scientific computing. However, existing methods rely on numerical solvers or autoregressive models that advance one small step at a time, which makes long horizons expensive. We instead view this problem as learning the system's time-invariant evolution operator, which jumps the state across a large time span in a single evaluation. To this end, we derive the consistency equations a time-invariant operator must satisfy, with differential and compositional objectives in physical time. These equations also connect the learned operator to the physics-prescribed instant dynamics, enabling physics embedding in consistency learning. Across five chaotic systems, we find that physics-distilled consistency makes both short-term trajectories and long-term statistics more accurate. The learned operator survives temporal extrapolation and requires one-tenth as many evaluations as autoregressive rollout, offering an efficient route to long-term simulation of chaotic dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Lufang Chiang, Jiachen Yao, Thomas Y. L. Lin, Anima Anandkumar
